source_snapshot.procedure: Labels a Fatal injection and provides split railtype9/voltagetype0/dimm0 lines for all DIMMs and voltage types0/1 without a power-action rule.
source_snapshot.criteria: Calls the event correctable and requires tool PASS plus OS report.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; generic PowerGood text does not establish signal polarity, rail voltage, timing or target.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Adds monitoring but leaves severity, PGOOD polarity, parameter meaning, 1.8V limits and dependent-function recovery undefined.

old_problem: Fatal/correctable semantics conflict; railtype9, voltage parameters and PGOOD fault polarity are unproven, the fixed split tuple lacks a full PMIC map, and no 1.8V/timing/reset/dependency/recovery oracle exists.
disposition_reason: PowerGood polarity, electrical tolerance and reset behavior are core stimulus and verdict semantics. ED-03/12/15/16/18 prohibit inferring them or executing a potentially logic-power-dropping fault without independent evidence and recovery, so this remains Pending/BLOCKED.
decision_basis: Read row97/history2495 and separated its 1.8V PGOOD coverage from row96 thermal warning and row98 current warning.
Preserved railtype9, both voltage types, every DIMM, fatal label, correctable criterion and OS evidence.
Required synchronized calibrated 1.8V and PGOOD capture because I2C may disappear if PMIC logic power drops.
Required dependent PMIC functions, DIMM training and memory health after reassertion.
No polarity, syntax, timeout or reset inference and no DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: DDR5 PMIC 1.8V LDO PowerGood transition and recovery
test_case.purpose: For each mapped PMIC, inject one approved 1.8V LDO/PGOOD transition, prove the exact signal polarity, rail behavior and authorized severity/reset outcome, then restore PGOOD, dependent functions and memory health.
required_package: Vendor railtype9, parameter and PGOOD polarity definition
Approved fatal/correctable severity and reset/no-reset policy
1.8V tolerance, PGOOD assert/deassert timing and abort limits
Complete tuple, independent capture, durable evidence and restoration procedure
test_case.test_command: Do not execute the ambiguous tuple. After approval, baseline calibrated 1.8V, PGOOD, raw status, I2C dependencies and memory; inject one exact mapped target once with independent capture; correlate the authorized transition and event; clear/restore only by the signed procedure and verify rail, dependencies and memory before another target.
test_case.expected_result: The intended 1.8V rail and PGOOD signal follow the signed polarity/timing and severity/reset contract, fresh target-specific evidence is preserved even if I2C drops, and PGOOD reasserts with stable 1.8V, normal dependent functions, all DIMMs and clean memory.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires physical target identity, calibrated voltage plus PGOOD timing, approved power action, fresh event and complete reassertion/recovery. A log alone, guessed polarity, unsafe voltage, unexpected reset, lost interface/DIMM or incomplete restoration fails.
safety_gate: Instrumented isolated SUT with independent OOB and calibrated 1.8V/PGOOD capture.
Abort on unsafe voltage, wrong polarity/timing, unapproved reset, I2C/dependency loss or memory error.
No automatic clear, reset or retry.
expected_evidence: Calibrated voltage, signal, status and memory baseline
Exact tuple plus synchronized voltage/PGOOD/OOB chronology
Fresh PMIC/CPER/SEL evidence through an independent path if I2C drops
Stable reassertion, dependency health, full DIMM/memory results and restoration diff
test_case.recovery: Preserve electrical and status evidence, then restore the LDO/PGOOD and PMIC configuration only through the approved path. Restore SPD/telemetry, I2C and BIOS/HDT, verify 1.8V stability, dependent functions, all DIMMs and bounded memory. Do not retry a failed recovery.

source_conflict.reason: Fatal/correctable conflict, unstated PGOOD polarity, fixed tuple population and absent voltage/timing/reset criteria remain unresolved.

blocked.reason: A wrong 1.8V/PGOOD action can remove PMIC logic and evidence access, reset the host or destabilize memory without a proven recovery path.
